result.summary: Modular-Monolith architecture with 4 services on None

output.overview: The modernized architecture translates the legacy VB6 banking application into a C# modular monolith, leveraging Docker for local deployment. The system preserves existing business logic while transitioning to a service-oriented architecture to enhance scalability and maintainability.

services.name: UI Service
services.responsibility: Render and manage user interfaces converted from VB6 forms to C# Windows Forms or WPF.

services.name: Business Logic Service
services.responsibility: Encapsulate and execute business logic previously embedded in VB6 forms.

services.name: Data Access Service
services.responsibility: Manage database interactions and data persistence.

services.name: Security Service
services.responsibility: Handle authentication, authorization, and security checks.

security.encryption: AES-256 for data at rest, TLS for data in transit

auto_scaling_rules: Scale out additional instances when CPU usage > 70%

data_flow.description: User interactions are sent to the business logic service for processing.
Business logic requests data operations from the data access service.
Data access service performs CRUD operations on the database.
Security service validates user credentials and issues tokens for authenticated sessions.

latency_optimizations: Use of in-memory caching with Redis to reduce database load
Minimize data transfer size between services
Optimize database queries with indexing and query tuning

trade_offs.decision: Use a modular monolith instead of microservices
trade_offs.rationale: Simplifies deployment and reduces overhead for a local Docker-based environment.

trade_offs.decision: Use REST APIs for service communication
trade_offs.rationale: Easier integration with existing systems and tools.
Sufficient for local development and testing, aligns with deployment target preference.

legacy_system.current_logic_summary: The legacy system is a VB6 application with multiple forms and ActiveX controls, handling various banking operations.
key_logic_steps: User logs in through the login form.
User navigates to the desired operation form (e.g., deposit, withdrawal).
User inputs data and triggers form events (e.g., button clicks).
ActiveX controls handle specific UI interactions and data binding.
Business logic is executed within the form event handlers.
